plan_a_advantages: More focused hill training to build trail-specific strength.
Shorter, more frequent long runs promote greater endurance development.
Includes a dedicated hill workout (55 min) which is crucial for trail running.
plan_b_advantages: Includes a tempo run to improve lactate threshold.
Longer duration easy runs could be beneficial for a runner who needs to build a larger aerobic base initially.
reasoning: Plan A is better suited for a trail runner aiming to become faster because it incorporates more targeted hill work and shorter, more frequent long runs. This approach directly addresses the demands of trail running – navigating varied terrain and building the specific muscular endurance required for uphill sections. Plan B, while including a tempo run, relies heavily on easy runs, which, while beneficial for base building, won't significantly improve speed or the ability to handle the intensity of a trail race. Plan A’s structured hill sessions and varied long run durations are more directly aligned with improving trail running performance.
